extracted.intended_audience: policy makers, public finance analysts, government economists, and legislators studying Quebec sovereignty and fiscal succession
extracted.subtask_short: pro forma fiscal analysis for Quebec sovereignty
extracted.subtask_description: Methodology and assumptions for constructing pro forma public‑finance statements for a newly sovereign Quebec, including rules for allocating federal revenues, expenses, assets and liabilities under alternative scenarios and sensitivity analyses. The page prescribes how to build scenarios, calculate deficits, service of debt, and net financing needs for a reference year (1990–1991).

rubrics_metrics.name: Revenus récupérés (assumption)
rubrics_metrics.description: Postulate that the revenues presently collected by the federal government on Québec territory would be collected by the Québec government (i.e. 'les revenus présentement perçus par le gouvernement fédéral sur le territoire québécois le seraient par le gouvernement du Québec').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute pro forma revenues by starting from current Québec revenues, subtracting lost federal transfer receipts, and adding federal revenues collected on Québec territory (example figures: revenus actuels 33,571M; moins transferts fédéraux perdus 6,797M; plus revenus fédéraux prélevés sur le Québec 24,461M → revenus pro forma ~51,235M).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dépenses additionnelles à assumer (assumption)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume Québec would assume federal expenditures currently performed for Québec residents (i.e. 'le Québec assumerait... les dépenses présentement effectuées par le gouvernement fédéral au bénéfice des Québécois').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate additional expenditures by category (transfers to individuals/enterprises/local governments; operating; capital). Provide scenarios with and without rationalization; example: dépenses additionnelles ≈18,163M (scénario I) added to current dépenses 35,551M → dépenses pro forma 53,714M.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ventilation des dépenses par grandes catégories
rubrics_metrics.description: Break down additional federal expenditures that Québec would assume into major categories: transfers to individuals/enterprises/local governments; operating expenditures; capital expenditures (e.g. 'des quelque 18 milliards... environ les deux tiers correspondent à des paiements de transferts..., tandis que l'autre tiers concerne des dépenses de fonctionnement').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report proportions and absolute amounts; note that within operating expenditures, personnel costs may exceed half and should be separately identified (example: personnel ≈3,000M, 18% of federal operating at that chapter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scénarios de dépenses: aucune rationalisation vs exemples de rationalisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct at least two spending scenarios: (1) no rationalization; (2) include plausible rationalizations (the report uses two specific examples: transport & communications expenses and the federal Revenue Ministry). Also use a 'moyenne' scenario equal to the average of the two.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare results across scenarios; when differences are small, use the scenario moyen for main analysis. Explicitly document which rationalizations are included and their numerical effects (example: two rationalizations reduce expenses by 522M and lower new expenditures to 24,438M when combined with lost revenues).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationalisation — transport et communications (method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate savings by comparing cost per employee for transport & communications between the federal norm and the Québec norm, applying the federal per‑capita norm to employees assigned to international affairs and the Québec norm to other Québec‑based employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute per‑employee cost differences and multiply by employee counts; the report example yields estimated total savings of ≈233M by assigning per‑capita norms by employee type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationalisation — ministère fédéral du Revenu (method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate Québec's share of customs/duties collection costs by the share of duties collected in Québec; raise Québec revenue‑department per‑taxpayer cost from current provincial level toward the Canadian per‑taxpayer cost to simulate nationwide collection costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply an upward adjustment to Québec's revenue department costs (example: increase per‑taxpayer cost from $70 to $93 → add $75M in costs; this alternative assumption reduced expenditures by 289M relative to the first scenario). Document whether customs collection and domestic tax collection are treated separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Règle de partage des bilans de succession (principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose that the share of passifs the Québec government would assume be directly proportional to the share of assets it would inherit (i.e. 'la part des passifs... soit directement proportionnelle à la part des actifs dont il hériterait').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement two federal succession balance sheets corresponding to two creditor classes: market bondholders and pension beneficiaries. Apply the proportional rule to allocate liabilities and compute resulting service‑of‑debt impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traitement séparé des comptes de pension (requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate the allocation and treatment of government‑sponsored pension accounts from other financial liabilities (the report treats pension accounts as a distinct creditor category; e.g. Québec's share of pension accounts estimated at 13.3%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute the implied additional debt service from assumed pension obligations (example: Québec share ≈9,456M → interest service ≈939M in 1990–1991).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hypothèses sur la valorisation des actifs non financiers (scenario design)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize substantial uncertainty in non‑financial asset valuations; build rechange scenarios by varying both the valuation level and the Québec share of those assets (scenarios A/B/C: base 72B with 18% Québec share; B: value set to $1; C: value increased to 108B and Québec share reduced to 15%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify how changes in asset valuations and Québec shares alter the pro forma accumulated deficit and Québec's share of federal debt. Present detailed tables (e.g., tableau 29, 30) showing impacts on debt service and deficit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of certain federal asset income (assumption)
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat profits of the Bank of Canada and the foreign exchange fund as federal property that Québec would not inherit (i.e. Québec is not assumed to be a shareholder in the Bank of Canada in a de facto monetary union).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude these profit items from Québec pro forma revenues; document consequent absence of corresponding liabilities or interest obligations (but note possible offsets in reduced liabilities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Calcul du service de la dette incluant passifs hérités
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute the increase in debt service by adding interest costs arising from the portion of federal debt and pension liabilities that Québec is assumed to inherit (example: service de la dette increases by ~7,104M; total service goes from 4,434M to 11,538M).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include both interest on inherited direct debt and interest/cost implications of assumed pension liabilities; reflect these in budgetary pro forma expenditures and deficits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Séparation opérations budgétaires et non budgétaires
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish budgetary operations (revenues and expenditures) from non‑budgetary operations (loans, capital endowments, advances, pensions, other) when computing net financing needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for the fact that some additional deficits are non‑cash and increase non‑budgetary balances rather than immediate market borrowing (example: 822M of pension commitments added to non‑budgetary operations reduces market borrowing needs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyse de sensibilité (required tests)
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform sensitivity analysis on key parameters: interest rates, expenditure levels, and the Québec share of the succession balance sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify impacts: a 100bp change in interest rates produces a specified deficit impact (example: one‑year 100bp → ≈519M; permanent 1% → ≈963.6M), a 1% change in pro forma expenditures → ≈490M deficit change, a one percentage‑point change in Québec share of the succession balance → ≈333M impact. Use static framework (reference year 1990–1991).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a static reference year (limitation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct the pro forma analysis in a static framework using a single reference year (1990–1991) and hold economic aggregates (e.g., GDP) fixed; do not model dynamic economic responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly note that dynamic effects (changes in GDP, tax base reactions, macroeconomic feedback) are not analyzed and thus sensitivity to GDP evolution cannot be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of results in absolute and relative terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Report pro forma deficits, net financing needs, and other aggregates both in monetary units (millions of dollars) and as percentages of GDP (e.g., déficit pro forma -9,282M = 5.8% of GDP in scenario A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide tables (e.g., tableaux 26–34) comparing scenarios A/B/C, and include indicators such as deficit/GDP, net financing needs (millions and % GDP), and debt/GDP ratios for comparability with other jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounting for low profitability of inherited state enterprises
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that inherited stakes in a small number of state enterprises (transports, communications) generate little placement income; therefore revenues from asset sharing are expected to be small (example: ≈40M).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not overstate asset‑income benefits; separately itemize expected revenues from inherited public enterprises and exclude those federal profit items Québec would not inherit (Bank of Canada, foreign exchange fund).

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel expense allocation by employee share
rubrics_metrics.description: Allocate federal personnel expenses to Québec proportionally to the share of federal employees working in Québec (example: number of federal employees in Québec = 18% → personnel expense share ≈18% of federal personnel costs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use employee counts and per‑employee cost norms to estimate Québec's personnel expenditure burden after succession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations and requirement for program reorganization for deeper savings
rubrics_metrics.description: State that deeper expenditure rationalizations require an in‑depth program‑by‑program analysis and a refonte of multiple programs, including taxation and social security systems; such structural choices are beyond the scope of the present working paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document that the present estimates assume maintenance of current service levels and that achieving larger savings would necessitate explicit policy choices and program redesigns, which must be modeled separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of negotiation and scheduling of debt assumption
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that the actual assumption of a share of federal debt could be negotiated and scheduled; the analysis models a negotiated commitment by Québec to pay interest on an agreed share but treats the debt legally as remaining a federal obligation to external creditors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When modeling cash‑flow impacts, allow for alternative timing/schedules of payments and note legal vs. fiscal treatment distinctions; present results under the assumption Québec commits to pay interest on the negotiated share.
